extracted.intended_audience: Researchers reporting health economic evaluations; journal editors and peer reviewers assessing economic evaluations for publication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reporting economic evaluations of health interventions for publication, aimed at improving completeness and transparency so editors, reviewers, and decision-makers can assess study quality and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS 24-item checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Out of 44 candidate items, 24 items and accompanying recommendations were developed. The recommendations are contained in a user friendly, 24 item checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist consolidates and updates previous health economic evaluation reporting guidance. A copy of the statement, accompanying checklist, and this report can be found on the ISPOR Health Economic Evaluations Publication Guidelines Task Force website. The aim is to lead to better reporting and ultimately better health decisions; the checklist is being co-published across multiple journals to facilitate dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: economic evaluations of health interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic evaluations of health interventions pose a particular challenge for reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CHEERS statement is targeted at studies performing economic evaluations of health interventions and is intended to improve the quality and transparency of reporting in this specific domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development methodology and evidence base
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of possible items based on a systematic review was created. A two round, modified Delphi panel consisting of representatives from academia, clinical practice, industry, government, and the editorial community was conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The need for new reporting guidance was identified by a survey of medical editors. The use of a systematic review and a multidisciplinary modified-Delphi process underpins the checklist's content and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination, endorsement, and update plan
rubrics_metrics.description: To facilitate dissemination and uptake, the CHEERS statement is being co-published across 10 health economics and medical journals. The author team plans to review the checklist for an update in five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals and groups are encouraged to endorse CHEERS to promote consistent reporting; the checklist is intended to be periodically reviewed and updated to remain current.
